key_insight: On a fixed compact manifold, parallel transport convolution is continuous in L² under C² perturbations of the Riemannian metric, subject to the stated localization and transport-path conventions.
engineering_relevance: The theorem provides a qualitative robustness foundation for geometric convolution layers when the underlying manifold geometry is slightly perturbed.
method: Estimate perturbations of geodesics, parallel transport, Jacobi fields, and exponential maps.
Compare transported kernels using uniform estimates away from the cut locus and integral bounds on small-volume neighborhoods.
Control changes in the Riemannian volume measure.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical continuity result for continuous inputs and continuous reference kernels with sufficiently localized support, not empirical benchmarks.
watch_item: The result gives qualitative continuity rather than an explicit robustness rate and requires the specified kernel localization and transport-path conventions.
paper_title: Stability of Parallel Transport Convolution under Riemannian Metric Perturbations
